lectures.title: Expanding Strings of Characters: the Brace Expansion `{...}`

cues.en: Let's now have a look at the brace expansion as of Bash four.
It's possible also to automatically expand strings of characters through the so-called brace expansion.
For example, this one here would expand and it would take both of those items.
So, for example, I could write something like this.
Echo data dot curly braces.
CSV, comma txt.
Curly braces closed.
And this would then expand to data dot csv and data dot txt and this would then be outputted.
So here we can see what will be outputted by our echo.
If I execute this here, we can see this here that I can just do data dot and then for example txt csv
for example, and then we can see how those items then are generated.
Of course we can combine this.
So for example here I could for example, use my single quotes or I could also use a variable expansion
here or a file name expansion and somewhere else.
So this works really well.
Also with all the other features that we have seen, if this brace expansion doesn't work for you,
then most likely you are running an older version of Bash.
For example, Mac by default still ships with Bash and version three point something because of license
restrictions.
And then of course, this brace expansion is not available.
Another way to use it that we can also let this brace expansion generate characters for us.
So, for example, here we could generate the whole alphabet or for example, here in lower cases.
And this is also really useful.
So if we want to use this, then I could, for example, do something like this A to Z.
I want to generate that.
And then I could for example, also add a dot txt at the end.
And then if I wanted to create all of those files at once, I could just put a touch in front and then
we can see how we have now created all of those files.
So this brace expansion can be extremely useful.
Brace expansion does not work within quotes, so it doesn't work in double quotes, nor does it work
in single quotes.
So this brace expansion cannot be within quotes.
But what would work, of course, would be if the rest of our expression is within quotes, that would
be totally allowed.
Just it's just important that our brace expansion itself is not within quotes and then everything should
work.
So this would be the brace expansion.
It's a really handy feature if you want to create lots, lots, lots of files or if you don't want to
write multiple file endings manually, then brace expansion can be extremely useful.
